resolutions: Object meaning is chosen by the user; objective case and prominence are derived by grammar.
ne, tē, tla, va1, and va2 are grammatical outputs rather than raw user controls.
c, qu, and qui are contextual realizations of the same third-person object morph.
Stem vowels in ca, tiqui, and que are not reassigned to the object carrier.
The tē/tla contrast is human versus nonhuman, not animate versus nonanimate.
English him, her, and it readings do not add grammatical gender to Nahuatl.
Reflexive object person and number are copied from the subject rather than independently selected.
Reciprocal meaning is allowed with plural subjects and blocked with singular subjects.
